verdicts.note: Chief deputy coroner since 2023, about 25 years at the sheriff's office including homicide and suspicious-death investigations, and a promise of 'a seamless transition' (S1). This is the insider continuity case for an open seat. -1, not -2, because he has never held the office or any elected post (S1). High confidence fits a documented career record. S2 (Lincoln Day dinner) adds little, but S1 alone carries the score.

+2 is the maximal outsider/renewal pole. She is new to the office and to elected office (S1, S5), and she argues 'you don't have to be a deputy to be a coroner' (S3). But she does not campaign on renewal, change or generational turnover. Her case is a credentials case: a nurse since 1989, nurse practitioner for 24 years, former hospice nurse, VA provider and IACME member (S1, S2, S3). Being an outsider to the office fits +1. Nothing in the dossier makes her the full renewal pole.

'I am fiscally conservative,' citing the county's $2 million deficit and promising a cost-control plan (S1), and 'careful spending' with 'every tax dollar' (S2). There is contrary evidence the score does not cite: she proposes more deputy coroners or volunteers to shorten rural response times (S3), which could add cost. Because she offers volunteers as an alternative, that proposal does not clearly cut against restraint. -1 at medium holds; the plan's details are unpublished.
